summary: T1-06 round 2: all three story checks pass. The committed cop30 record and the ProductRecord match the saved raw ranges. Both round-1 fixes (codex-r1-1 and codex-r1-2) are in place and tested. I found no blocker or high finding. The only paths changed outside the story's files list are log, review and batch bookkeeping files.

checks.evidence: 1411 passed, 2 xfailed. The two xfails are the T1-01 schema-case fixtures, unrelated to this story.

checks.criterion: Check: uv run python -m terraluna_pipeline.pilot check cop30
checks.command: uv run python -m terraluna_pipeline.pilot check cop30

checks.evidence: ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed (24 files), mypy reported no issues in 24 source files.

checks.criterion: AC1: deterministic tile, credential-free HTTPS URL, header and window read by range request, readers in io.py
checks.evidence: cop30_range_read.json range_read.url is https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/..., with whole_file_downloaded false and 3 requests. The io.py diff adds the COG layout and remote readers. Tests cover an absent tile with a recorded fallback (test_pilot_cop30.py:956) and a tile choice the list does not support (:1057). I did not re-check the tile's presence in the saved tileList.txt by hand; the record reads the tile list from the saved file.

The record states the URL, HTTP 206, Content-Range 'bytes 0-262143/19059689', object size 19059689, bytes requested and received 2883584, the COG structure, CRS EPSG:4326, pixel size, vertical datum (file 'unknown', product docs EGM2008 quoted), nodata null with a note, units from the product docs, valid_fraction 1.0, elevation min 715.64 and max 806.08. surface_model_caveat is a top-level key.

checks.criterion: AC3: 5 km window, bytes, tiles touched, budget observation
checks.evidence: window.side_m 5000 at a stated centre with centre_basis disclosed. live_probe_budget has bytes_fetched 2883584, limit 4000000, tiles_touched 1 and within_budget true. The record does not claim an observed centre.

checks.criterion: AC4: ProductRecord upserted into sources.json with licence, sha256 and local_path
checks.evidence: The added entry has license_or_attribution quoted from the provider pages, checksum 2f8ad7cf... equal to range_read.local_sha256, and local_path data/raw/cop30/Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N64_00_W017_00_DEM.tif.ranges. The file exists at 2883584 bytes, which equals bytes_received. verification_status is PARTIAL, not overstated. I did not confirm the sort order by reading the whole file.

checks.criterion: AC5: unreachable bucket fails non-zero naming the URL and error
checks.evidence: Tests at test_pilot_cop30.py:589, 602 and 615 cover an unreachable bucket, document and tile, and a refused connection, each naming the URL. All pass in the full run.

checks.criterion: AC6: fetch saves tileList.txt, ranges and HTTP metadata; record and check run offline
checks.evidence: data/raw/cop30 holds tileList.txt, the .ranges file, fetch.json and the provider pages. check cop30 passes offline against the committed outputs.

checks.criterion: Round-1 fix codex-r1-1: unstated tile sizes stay unknown
checks.evidence: Commit 1f88300 adds the failing sparse-COG tests: the test_io_cog_layout.py stored_bytes table and test_pilot_cop30.py::test_a_touched_tile_the_file_does_not_store_has_unknown_bytes. Both run and pass in the full suite. The record's touched_tile_bytes definition says it is null when a size is unstated.

checks.criterion: Round-1 fix codex-r1-2: licence quote from visible text
checks.evidence: The same commit adds the visible-text tests (JSON-LD decoys in script, style and comments). They pass. The committed sources.json licence string is a full sentence from the visible page, not escaped JSON-LD.

findings.claim: The range also touches logs/agents/*, reviews/* and scripts/ralph/batches/t1-pilot/{prd.json,progress.txt}, which are not in the story's files list.
findings.evidence: These are agent logs, review records and batch bookkeeping. config/ and PRD.md are unchanged, so no kickoff values were set and no gate was passed. This agrees with the round-1 rebuttal.

findings.claim: The window centre comes from a Wikipedia coordinate that was not fetched, so it is a stated choice and not an observation.
findings.evidence: The record discloses this and the criterion asks for a stated centre. No config/run.yaml values are set. The record is acceptable as written.
